components.text: The large plant count misses much distributed solar, so this report uses the full count.

footnote: Source: National Bureau of Statistics of China (Jan, Feb 2026)
notes: The full count comes from the annual statistical communiqué. The large-plant count covers industrial enterprises above designated size. The two should not be mixed. On the full count, thermal output fell 0.7% and solar rose 39.8%. On the large-plant count solar rose only 24.4%, mostly because distributed solar is left out. Other readings: the China Electricity Council puts coal power output down 1.9%, with coal at 51.1% of generation, and calculates that new wind, solar and bioenergy output equalled 97.1% of the rise in power use. China's total power use was 10,368 TWh, up 5.0%.
